glossary.definition: An AI agent that acts for a customer: it asks for a balance, a transfer, an order. Simulated in mock; the use case is from the AI-DEMO2 catalog, the amounts and events are lab-invented.

RFC 8693 token exchange mints a delegated token whose sub is the customer and whose act claim names the agent. Delegation, not impersonation. Simulated in mock; the use case is from the AI-DEMO2 catalog, the amounts and events are lab-invented.
The customer lets a named agent act for them before the exchange. Simulated in mock; the use case is from the AI-DEMO2 catalog, the amounts and events are lab-invented.

A policy decision on every call: PERMIT, DENY, or an obligation (step-up, human approval, CIBA). The lab's thresholds are lab-invented, fitted to the catalog's example amounts. Simulated in mock; the use case is from the AI-DEMO2 catalog, the amounts and events are lab-invented.

A risky write returns an obligation instead of running: MFA step-up, or a verified human approval receipt. A boolean "approved" flag from the client does not count. Simulated in mock; the use case is from the AI-DEMO2 catalog, the amounts and events are lab-invented.

The agent asks the identity provider to authenticate the customer on another device and polls until they approve. Needs a live feature flag; runs in mock here. Simulated in mock; the use case is from the AI-DEMO2 catalog, the amounts and events are lab-invented.

The gateway validates signature, audience, expiry, act claim and scope, applies rate limits and edge policy, and fails closed. Simulated in mock; the use case is from the AI-DEMO2 catalog, the amounts and events are lab-invented.

A nested act claim when one agent hands work to another: scope is narrowed at each hop and an unregistered agent in the chain is denied. Simulated in mock; the use case is from the AI-DEMO2 catalog, the amounts and events are lab-invented.

Simulated in mock; in live (the owner's opt-in) a run makes two real calls to one PingOne environment: its discovery document and the agent's own client-credentials token (shown masked). It runs nothing else: no customer sign-in, token exchange, gateway check, policy decision or tool call, and it lists the steps it did not run. The path has not been run against a real tenant by the builder: UNVERIFIED.
Every token in this lab is issued by the lab, labelled MOCK and signed ES256 with a public mock key. It protects nothing and is shown raw for education.

cards.label: Why it matters: a customer-facing agent that cannot overreach
cards.description: Challenge: Appfire's HIVE platform already manages the backend: data policy and which MCP servers may be used. The open question is the agent-facing front end: who or what the agent is, what it is allowed to do, under which conditions, and how each decision is enforced and recorded — without a person approving every step. Technical: Ping governs the front end: the agent gets its own identity, receives delegated privileges (RFC 8693 act chain), and every tool call, MCP-server hop and data access gets a policy decision with a risk-based outcome — auto-allow for low-risk reads, step-up or human approval for risky writes, deny for out-of-scope actions — all enforced at the tool, data and action layers, not left to the model. Business: Controlled autonomy: low-risk actions proceed inside policy, higher-risk ones are constrained or approved, and every decision leaves an audit record naming the agent, the principal it acted for, the resource and the decision — the visibility Appfire's AI Governance program is asking for, complementing (not replacing) HIVE. (Lab summary of the AI-DEMO2 catalog text, not a Ping claim.)

cards.description: Mock runs a whole use case offline. Live, which the owner switches on, reaches the identity provider only and lists what it did not run. UNVERIFIED on a real tenant.
